queued_state_order: GSLevel::LoadLevel stores request values and calls StateMachine::SwitchState
SwitchState appends a queued operation; it does not synchronously pop the active GSLevel
_switchState calls _popAllState before _pushState, so old GSLevel teardown precedes destination construction
GSLevel destructor calls Level::Unload, closes HUD, deletes old Level, then clears GSLevel::s_level
Level::Unload calls QuickSave(Level+0xf0); after Application::LoadLevel reset Level state to zero, QuickSave state-38 gate skips without serializers

Level::Unload pushes loading UI, deletes optional Level fields +0x128 then +0x12c, calls SG_SaveAllPlayer(Level+0xf0), stops sounds with 500ms, conditionally pops loading UI, clears state, network-uninitializes ObjectManager, updates PlayerManager, and resets RNG to real-time seed/zero synchronized seed
StateMachine updates the new top state after draining the operation and toggles the updating flag around its update callback
owner_boundary: The adapter borrows the existing old GSLevel, Level, LevelSavegame, ObjectManager, PlayerManager and StateMachine identities. It routes QuickSave through the existing level_quick_save_v1 kernel and leaves SaveAllPlayer, Level cleanup, state construction, and destination update to providers. It owns no queue, Save, Level, or renderer scene.
validation: Host fixture composes the existing QuickSave kernel and checks the state-zero skip, preserved force byte for SaveAllPlayer, old-state teardown order, destination request identity, update guard, and no replay after destructive handoff. This is source-order adapter evidence, not runtime gameplay parity.
